mainTopic: End of the משנה on doubtful ox-damage claims (המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה), the debate over whether it argues with סומכוס, and רבה בר נתן's wheat-and-barley rule
overview: The amud finishes the משנה about oxen that chased and hurt another ox when nobody knows which one did the damage. When the owner and the injured party argue over which ox did it (large or small, תם or מועד, or which ox hurt which), the rule is המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה: whoever wants to take money must bring proof. רבי חייא בר אבא learns from this that the חכמים disagree with סומכוס, who splits doubtful money even when both sides claim to be certain. רב פפא objects. If the משנה is a case where both sides are certain, its סיפא would contradict רבה בר נתן's rule that someone sued for wheat who admits to barley is fully exempt. So the גמרא reads the סיפא as ניזק שמא ומזיק ברי and the רישא as ניזק ברי ומזיק שמא, and explains that these count as one kind of case. Then the גמרא examines רבה בר נתן's rule itself and challenges it from our משנה. It answers that the injured party is only 'fit to take' and the court does not collect for him, and that a ברייתא saying he is paid speaks of a case where he already grabbed. The amud ends with the same challenge raised from the תם and מועד case, which is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Two owners are exempt, one owner is liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends the case of two oxen chasing one ox. If they belong to two different people, both owners are exempt. If both belong to one person, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them are exempt. If both oxen belonged to one person, both are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה in the middle. It is finishing the case where two oxen chased one ox, and the injured owner cannot say which one hurt his ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the two oxen have different owners, each owner can say, "Prove it was my ox." So nobody pays. When both oxen belong to the same person, he cannot escape that way, so he is liable. The גמרא will explain this later.

keyTerms.meaning: exempt, do not have to pay
liable, must pay
one person (a single owner)

phrases.english: The two of them are exempt.
If both of them were
of one person,
both are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous amud (35a).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two owners whose oxen chased: both exempt. One owner of both oxen: liable.

steps.title: Arguing over which of one owner's oxen did the damage
steps.stepSummary: Both chasing oxen belong to one owner. The injured party says the ox that would make him pay more did it, and the owner says the cheaper one did. The person claiming money must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say one ox was large and one was small. The injured party says, "The large one did the damage," and the owner says, "No, the small one did." Or say one was a תם and one was a מועד. The injured party says, "The מועד did it," and the owner says, "No, the תם did." The one who wants to take money from his fellow must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two cases where the owner of both oxen agrees he must pay, but argues about how much. It rules that the claimant must bring proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תם pays only half the damage, and only up to the value of that ox. So a large ox means a bigger possible payment than a small one, and a מועד pays full damage. Since it is a doubt, the money stays with the owner unless the injured party proves his claim.

keyTerms.meaning: an ox not yet known to gore; pays half damages from its own body
a forewarned ox that has gored before; pays full damages
the injured party
the one responsible for the damage (the owner)
the one taking money from another must bring proof

steps.whatToRemember: In a doubtful damage claim, the money stays where it is. The one who wants to collect must prove his side.

the injured party says: "The large one did the damage,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the one-owner case and asks how much he pays when the two sides argue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the two sides argue over which ox did the damage, the burden of proof is on the claimant.

steps.title: Two injured oxen and two damaging oxen
steps.stepSummary: Now two oxen were hurt and two oxen did the hurting. The sides argue about which ox hurt which. Again, the claimant must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the injured oxen were two, one large and one small, and the damaging oxen were two, one large and one small. The injured party says, "The large one hurt the large one, and the small one hurt the small one." The owner says, "No, the small one hurt the large one, and the large one hurt the small one." Or say one damaging ox was a תם and one a מועד. The injured party says, "The מועד hurt the large one, and the תם hurt the small one." The owner says, "No, the תם hurt the large one, and the מועד hurt the small one." The one who wants to take money from his fellow must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה makes the case harder: two injured oxen and two damaging oxen. It argues over the pairing, and gives the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The injured party pairs the oxen in the way that gets him the most money. He wants the big damage to come from the big ox, or from the מועד that pays in full. The owner pairs them the cheaper way. Even in this harder case, the rule does not change: the claimant must prove his version.

keyTerms.meaning: the injured animals
the animals that did the damage
"not so" — a denial of the other side's claim

one large and one small,
and the damaging ones were two —
one large and one small;

and the small one the small one,"
and the one liable for the damage says:

the one who takes money from his fellow, the proof is upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the same rule to a harder case with two injured oxen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when the dispute is over which ox hurt which, the claimant must bring proof.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה ends with one rule: המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה.

steps.title: The משנה shows the חכמים disagree with סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא learns from the משנה's rule (the claimant must bring proof) that סומכוס's colleagues reject his view that doubtful money is split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: This teaches that his colleagues disagree with סומכוס, who says that money whose ownership is in doubt is divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבי חייא בר אבא draws a conclusion from the משנה about a well-known argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס holds that when it is unclear who owns money, the two sides split it. Our משנה does not split the money in these doubtful cases. Instead it makes the claimant bring proof. So the author of the משנה must be the חכמים who disagree with סומכוס.

keyTerms.meaning: "this is to say" — introduces a conclusion drawn from a source
money whose ownership is in doubt
they divide it

steps.confusionAlert: "חלוקים" (they disagree) and "חולקין" (they divide) look alike but mean different things. The first is about the colleagues arguing; the second is סומכוס's rule of splitting the money.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next discussion: does the משנה really go against סומכוס, or can it be explained even according to him?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said:
That is to say
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words in square brackets and some don't. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: his colleagues disagree with him,
with Sumakhos,
phrases.notes: "Him" in the last line means סומכוס. The text names him only here.

phrases.english: who says:
money that lies in doubt —
they divide it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the משנה's repeated rule, המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה, which makes the claimant bring proof, follows the חכמים against סומכוס, who would split doubtful money.

steps.title: Does סומכוס split even when both sides are certain?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל asks רבי חייא בר אבא whether סומכוס splits doubtful money even when both sides make certain claims.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל said to רבי חייא בר אבא: Does סומכוס really say to split the money even when each side is sure of his claim?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל asks a clarifying question about רבי חייא בר אבא's statement from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר אבא said the משנה argues with סומכוס. But the משנה is a case where both sides are sure of what they say. So רבי אבא בר ממל asks: does סומכוס's rule of splitting really reach even that kind of case?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Certain and certain': both sides claim to know for sure

steps.confusionAlert: Splitting sounds most natural when nobody knows what happened. The question is whether סומכוס splits even when each side insists he knows for sure.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel said to Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba:
Does Sumakhos say this even when it is certain and certain?
phrases.notes: 'Certain and certain' means each side says he knows for sure what happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how far סומכוס's view goes, since רבי חייא בר אבא assumed the משנה argues with him
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether סומכוס's rule of splitting applies even when both parties make certain claims

steps.title: Yes, סומכוס splits even when both are certain
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא answers that סומכוס splits the money even in a case of בָּרִי וּבָרִי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered him: Yes. סומכוס says to split even when both sides are certain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers the question: סומכוס's rule covers even certain claims.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is what lets the משנה argue with סומכוס. If סומכוס only split in cases where nobody knows, a משנה about certain claims would have nothing to do with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets סומכוס's view at its widest: he splits doubtful money even when both sides claim to know for sure.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
Sumakhos says it even when it is certain and certain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סומכוס splits doubtful money even in a case of בָּרִי וּבָרִי

steps.title: How do we know the משנה is about certain claims?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what shows that the משנה is talking about a case where both sides are certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that our משנה is a case where both sides are certain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source in the משנה's wording showing that both sides are certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole idea that the משנה argues with סומכוס depends on reading it as בָּרִי וּבָרִי. So the גמרא wants to see where the משנה shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where (do we know)?
Our משנה

phrases.english: And from where do we know that our mishna is a case of certain and certain?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the reading of the משנה that the argument with סומכוס depends on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the משנה's wording shows that both sides make certain claims

steps.title: The wording 'this one says… that one says No' shows certainty
steps.stepSummary: The משנה has one side say 'Your ox did damage' and the other say 'No', which shows both sides are sure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it teaches: This one says, 'Your ox did the damage,' and that one says, 'No, it was not so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the משנה's wording: each side flatly states his claim, so both are certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who is not sure would say 'I don't know.' A firm statement followed by a firm denial ('No!') means both sides claim to know what happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it teaches (in the משנה)
'No, it was not so': a firm denial

phrases.english: Because it teaches: This one says, 'Your ox did the damage,'
and that one says, 'No, it was not so.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 using the משנה's wording
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The firm claim and firm denial in the משנה show it is a case of בָּרִי וּבָרִי

steps.title: רב פפא: if the first part is certain, so is the last part
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא starts a challenge: if the רישא of the משנה is בָּרִי וּבָרִי, the סיפא must be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenged this: Since the first part of the משנה is a case of certain claims, the last part must also be a case of certain claims.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins an attack on the claim that the משנה is בָּרִי וּבָרִי. He is setting up a problem he will show from the סיפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא accepts that both parts of a משנה should be read the same way. So if the רישא is about certain claims, the סיפא is too. He is about to show that reading the סיפא this way causes a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it: the opening of a strong objection
The first part of a משנה
The last part of a משנה

phrases.english: Rav Pappa challenged it:
Since the first part is certain and certain,
the last part is also certain and certain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the משנה as בָּרִי וּבָרִי that step 8 just proved
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה as a case of בָּרִי וּבָרִי (and so the proof that the חכמים argue with סומכוס)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both parts of a משנה should be read the same way, so the סיפא must also be בָּרִי וּבָרִי. The next step shows why that is a problem.

steps.title: רב פפא quotes the סיפא: big or small, תם or מועד
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא quotes the סיפא: when the two sides argue over which ox did the damage (big or small, תם or מועד), the claimant must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the סיפא: If one ox was big and one small, and the injured party says, 'The big one did the damage,' and the damager says, 'No, the small one did it'; or if one was a תם and one a מועד, and the injured party says, 'The מועד did it,' and the damager says, 'No, the תם did it': the one who wants to take money from his friend must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא quotes the סיפא of the משנה to build his challenge. This is setup: the main point of his question comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case in the סיפא has a firm claim and a firm denial, so by רב פפא's logic it is בָּרִי וּבָרִי. In each case, the owner of the damaging ox admits that one of his oxen did the damage; he only argues about which one. רב פפא will use this to show a difficulty with reading the משנה as certain claims.

keyTerms.meaning: The injured party
The one responsible for the damage (the owner of the oxen)
An ox with no history of goring; its owner pays half damages, only from the ox itself
An ox known to gore; its owner pays full damages
Whoever wants to take money from another must bring proof

steps.confusionAlert: The damager here is not denying everything. He admits his small ox, or his תם, did it. He is only arguing about which of his oxen did it, because that changes how much he pays.

phrases.english: Say the last part:
If one was big and one was small,
the injured party says, 'The big one did the damage,'

phrases.aramaic: וּמַזִּיק אוֹמֵר: ״לֹא כִי, אֶלָּא קָטָן הִזִּיק״;
phrases.english: and the damager says, 'No, rather the small one did the damage';
if one was a tam and one was a muad,
phrases.notes: A תם has no history of goring. A מועד is known to gore, so its owner pays more.

phrases.english: the injured party says, 'The muad did the damage,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהַמַּזִּיק אוֹמֵר: ״לֹא כִי, אֶלָּא תָּם הִזִּיק״ –
phrases.english: and the damager says, 'No, rather the tam did the damage':
the one who takes money from his fellow must bring the proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב פפא's challenge by quoting the סיפא he says must also be בָּרִי וּבָרִי
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the סיפא of the משנה as בָּרִי וּבָרִי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא has firm claims about which ox did the damage, so by the same reasoning it is בָּרִי וּבָרִי. רב פפא is setting this up to show a problem, which he states in steps 11 and 12.

steps.title: Inference from the סיפא: without proof, he collects what the מזיק admits
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reads the סיפא closely. The claimant must bring proof, so if he has none, he collects according to the מזיק's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: This tells us that if he does not bring proof, he takes what the one who did the damage says.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws an inference from the סיפא that he quoted in the last step. This is setting up his real attack in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the claimant must bring proof. That implies a second point: without proof, he is not left empty-handed. He gets paid according to what the מזיק admits, for example payment from the small ox.

keyTerms.meaning: proof
he takes, he collects
the one whose animal did the damage, the defendant

phrases.english: This implies: if he does not bring proof
he takes according to what the damager says;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from the סיפא quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה (and so also its סיפא) is a case of בָּרִי וּבָרִי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This sets up the premise: without proof, the ניזק collects what the מזיק admits. The next step shows why that is a problem.

steps.title: This would contradict רבה בר נתן
steps.stepSummary: If both sides are sure, the מזיק is admitting to something different from what was claimed, yet he pays. רבה בר נתן says such a person is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבה בר נתן? He said: if one claimed wheat from another, and the other admitted to owing him barley, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings his main attack. Read as בָּרִי וּבָרִי, the סיפא clashes with a ruling of רבה בר נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר נתן says that admitting to something other than what was claimed (barley instead of wheat) makes you פטור completely. In the סיפא, the ניזק claims 'the big ox did it' and the מזיק admits 'the small ox did it.' That is a different admission, yet the מזיק pays. If both are certain, this is exactly רבה בר נתן's case, and the משנה would argue with him.

keyTerms.meaning: a refutation, a strong challenge that disproves a view
he claimed from him
he admitted
exempt, does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Wheat and barley are just an example of 'he claimed one thing and the other admitted to a different thing.' Here, big ox and small ox play the same roles.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is a refutation
of רבה בר נתן
who said: if he claimed wheat from him
and the other admitted to him barley, he is exempt?
phrases.notes: He is פטור from the wheat because he denied it, and from the barley because nobody claimed it from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא תִּהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבָּה בַּר נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 11 to show a clash with רבה בר נתן.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the סיפא as בָּרִי וּבָרִי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a בָּרִי וּבָרִי case, the מזיק's admission (small ox) does not match the claim (big ox), yet he pays. That goes against רבה בר נתן, who says such a person is פטור.

steps.title: So the סיפא must be a case where one side is sure and one is unsure
steps.stepSummary: To avoid contradicting רבה בר נתן, the סיפא must be a case of בָּרִי וְשֶׁמָּא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is talking about a case of 'certain' and 'maybe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the סיפא cannot be בָּרִי וּבָרִי. One side is sure and the other only says 'maybe.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up רב פפא's point: if the סיפא is בָּרִי וְשֶׁמָּא, the רישא may be the same. That would undo the proof from step 8 that the משנה is a case of בָּרִי וּבָרִי. The next step asks exactly which side is the sure one.

keyTerms.meaning: one side claims with certainty, the other only says 'maybe'
rather, so it must be

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case of 'certain' and 'maybe.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem in step 12 by redefining the case of the סיפא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא is בָּרִי וּבָרִי, like the רישא was thought to be.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא is בָּרִי וְשֶׁמָּא, so it does not clash with רבה בר נתן.

steps.title: Who is sure and who is unsure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which party says 'certain' and which says 'maybe.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the one saying 'certain,' and who is the one saying 'maybe'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the new case. This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to set up בָּרִי וְשֶׁמָּא: either the ניזק is sure and the מזיק is unsure, or the other way around. The גמרא will test each option.

keyTerms.meaning: who?
the one who says

phrases.english: The one who says 'certain', who is it?
The one who says 'maybe', who is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקָאָמַר בָּרִי מַאן, דְּקָאָמַר שֶׁמָּא מַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details of the case proposed in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which party is certain and which party is unsure in the סיפא.

steps.title: If the injured party is sure, the problem with רבה בר נתן comes back
steps.stepSummary: If the ניזק is certain and the מזיק unsure, the מזיק still pays on a different admission. That again goes against רבה בר נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the injured party says 'certain' and the damager says 'maybe,' then let us still say it is a refutation of רבה בר נתן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and rejects it. With the ניזק sure, we are back to the same contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ניזק firmly claims the big ox did it, and the מזיק says the small ox maybe did it. The ניזק's firm claim is still different from what the מזיק admits, yet the מזיק pays from the small ox. That is the wheat-and-barley case again, so רבה בר נתן is still contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: the injured party, the claimant
still, even so

phrases.english: If we say the injured party says 'certain'
and the damager says 'maybe',
let us still say it is a refutation
of רבה בר נתן!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נֵימָא דְּקָאָמַר נִיזָּק בָּרִי וְקָאָמַר מַזִּיק שֶׁמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the ניזק is certain and the מזיק unsure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ניזק's firm claim (big ox) still does not match the admission (small ox), yet the מזיק pays. That contradicts רבה בר נתן just as before.

steps.title: The injured party is unsure and the damager is sure
steps.stepSummary: The case must be that the ניזק says 'maybe' and the מזיק says 'certain.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the injured party says 'maybe,' and the damager says 'certain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on the second option: the ניזק is unsure and the מזיק is certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ניזק only says 'maybe,' he is not firmly contradicting the מזיק's admission about the small ox. So the מזיק pays what he admitted, and this is not רבה בר נתן's case of a firm claim met by a different admission.

keyTerms.meaning: maybe, an unsure claim
certain, a sure claim

steps.whatToRemember: The סיפא is a case where the ניזק says 'maybe' and the מזיק says 'certain.' Read that way, it fits רבה בר נתן. It also challenges the earlier reading (step 8) that the משנה is a case of בָּרִי וּבָרִי.

phrases.english: Rather, the injured party says 'maybe',
and the damager says 'certain'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּקָאָמַר נִיזָּק שֶׁמָּא וְקָאָמַר מַזִּיק בָּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 15 rejects the first option, this gives the only option left.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The סיפא is בָּרִי וְשֶׁמָּא, with the ניזק unsure and the מזיק certain. This avoids any contradiction with רבה בר נתן.

steps.title: Inferring that the first clause matches the second clause
steps.stepSummary: Since the סיפא is ניזק שמא ומזיק ברי, the גמרא suggests the רישא is that same kind of case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since the סיפא is a case where the ניזק says 'maybe' and the מזיק says 'certain,' the רישא is also a case where the ניזק says 'maybe' and the מזיק says 'certain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes its conclusion about the סיפא and applies it to the רישא. This inference sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that both halves of a משנה are usually the same kind of case. So if the סיפא is ניזק שמא ומזיק ברי, the רישא should be too. This replaces the earlier idea that the רישא was a case where both sides are certain.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
The later clause of the משנה
The injured party says 'maybe' (he is not sure)
The one accused of damage says 'I am certain'

phrases.english: And since the latter clause is: the injured party says 'maybe' and the damager says 'certain,'

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא נָמֵי נִיזָּק שֶׁמָּא וּמַזִּיק בָּרִי;
phrases.english: the first clause is also: the injured party says 'maybe' and the damager says 'certain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion about the סיפא (Step 16) to define the רישא the same way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רישא, like the סיפא, is a case of ניזק שמא ומזיק ברי.

steps.title: Would סומכוס really split the money in such a weak claim?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: in a case where the ניזק only says 'maybe,' סומכוס would not say to split, so the משנה would have no reason to teach that we don't split.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does סומכוס say to split even in this kind of case, so that the משנה needs to teach us that we don't?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from Step 17. It says that reading makes the רישא pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא rules that the one taking money from his friend must bring proof, which argues against סומכוס, who says to split. But if the ניזק is only saying 'maybe' and the מזיק is certain, even סומכוס would agree the ניזק gets nothing. Then there is no argument left for the משנה to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
To teach us

phrases.english: And does Sumakhos say this even in such a case,
phrases.notes: He means סומכוס's rule that money in doubt is divided.

phrases.english: that it was necessary to teach us that we do not?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the רישא as ניזק שמא ומזיק ברי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In that case even סומכוס would not split the money, so the משנה's ruling would teach nothing new.

steps.title: The first clause is the reverse case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that only the סיפא is ניזק שמא ומזיק ברי, while the רישא is ניזק ברי ומזיק שמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The סיפא is a case where the ניזק says 'maybe' and the מזיק says 'certain.' But the רישא is a case where the ניזק says 'certain' and the מזיק says 'maybe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea that both clauses are the same case. It gives the רישא the opposite setup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the ניזק is certain and the מזיק is not sure, סומכוס would say to split. So the משנה does need to teach that the ניזק must bring proof. This brings back the purpose of the רישא.

keyTerms.meaning: The injured party says 'I am certain'
The damager says 'maybe' (he is not sure)
No (rejecting the previous suggestion)

steps.confusionAlert: In Step 15 a ניזק ברי ומזיק שמא case was rejected, but only for the סיפא, because of רבה בר נתן's rule. Here the גמרא gives that setup to the רישא, which is a different clause.

phrases.aramaic: לָא; סֵיפָא נִיזָּק שֶׁמָּא וּמַזִּיק בָּרִי,
phrases.english: No; the latter clause is: injured party 'maybe' and damager 'certain,'
but the first clause is: injured party 'certain' and damager 'maybe.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; סֵיפָא נִיזָּק שֶׁמָּא וּמַזִּיק בָּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18 by redefining the רישא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the רישא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא is the same as the סיפא: ניזק שמא ומזיק ברי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is ניזק ברי ומזיק שמא, a case where סומכוס would split, so the משנה's ruling is needed.

steps.title: Now the two clauses don't match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this answer makes the רישא and the סיפא two different kinds of cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then the רישא is not like the סיפא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 19. Under that answer, the two halves of the משנה describe opposite situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה normally keeps both clauses parallel. Now one clause is ניזק ברי ומזיק שמא and the other is the reverse. The גמרא sees this mismatch as a weakness in the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: But look (introducing an objection)
It is not similar
The first clause to the latter clause

phrases.english: But the first clause is not similar to the latter clause!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the רישא is ניזק ברי ומזיק שמא while the סיפא is ניזק שמא ומזיק ברי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two clauses of the משנה should describe the same kind of case, but under this answer they are opposites.

steps.title: Certain-and-maybe either way counts as one kind of case
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'certain and maybe' and 'maybe and certain' are one kind of case, unlike 'certain and certain' paired with 'maybe and certain'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: 'certain and maybe' and 'maybe and certain' are one matter. 'Certain and certain' and 'maybe and certain' are two matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 20, which said the רישא and סיפא had become two different kinds of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both the רישא (ניזק ברי ומזיק שמא) and the סיפא (ניזק שמא ומזיק ברי), one side is sure and the other side is unsure. Only the sides are swapped, so this is really one type of case. A רישא of ברי וברי next to a סיפא of שמא וברי would be two truly different types.

keyTerms.meaning: Certain. A sure claim.
Maybe. An unsure claim.
One matter. The same kind of case.
Two matters. Different kinds of cases.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's רישא is ניזק ברי ומזיק שמא and its סיפא is ניזק שמא ומזיק ברי. These count as one kind of case: one side sure, one side unsure.

phrases.english: They say:
"certain and maybe" and "maybe and certain"
phrases.notes: The first is the רישא as just explained (ניזק sure, מזיק unsure). The second is the סיפא.

phrases.english: are one matter;
"certain and certain" and "maybe and certain"
are two matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: בָּרִי וְשֶׁמָּא, שֶׁמָּא וּבָרִי – חַד מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 and defends the reading from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what counts as the same kind of case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making the רישא ברי ושמא and the סיפא שמא וברי splits the משנה into two unrelated cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are mixed cases with one side sure and one side unsure, so they count as one matter.

steps.title: רבה בר נתן: claimed wheat, admitted barley, exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבה בר נתן's rule: if one claims wheat and the other admits barley, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the matter itself. רבה בר נתן said: if he claimed wheat from him and the other admitted barley, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section and looks closely at רבה בר נתן's ruling, which came up earlier in the סוגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claimant asked for one thing (wheat), and the defendant admitted to a different thing (barley). רבה בר נתן rules that the defendant is exempt. The next steps will ask exactly what this rule adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא returns to examine a statement it mentioned earlier.
He claimed from him.
And he admitted to him.
Exempt.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rabba bar Natan said:
If he claimed wheat from him
and the other admitted to him about barley, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רישא/סיפא discussion and goes back to examine רבה בר נתן's ruling, which was quoted in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Claimed wheat, admitted barley: the defendant is exempt.

steps.title: This is already taught in a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבה בר נתן is adding, since a משנה already says this exact rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned: if he claimed wheat and the other admitted barley, he is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה בר נתן: why say a rule that already appears word for word in a משנה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's statement is expected to add something new. Since the משנה already has the identical wording, his statement seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? This asks what is new.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in שבועות 38b.

phrases.aramaic: טְעָנוֹ חִטִּין וְהוֹדָה לוֹ בִּשְׂעוֹרִין – פָּטוּר!
phrases.english: If he claimed wheat and the other admitted barley, he is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement in step 22 as adding nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already says the identical rule, so his statement seems to add nothing.

steps.title: He teaches that the defendant is fully exempt
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה alone we might think he still pays for the barley. רבה בר נתן teaches that he is completely exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that משנה, I would have said he is exempt from the value of the wheat but must pay the value of the barley. He teaches us that he is completely exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבה בר נתן is explaining how far the משנה's 'exempt' goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'exempt' in the משנה could mean only exempt from the wheat that was claimed. Then he would still owe the barley he admitted. רבה בר נתן says no: he owes nothing, not even the barley.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said. This is the mistaken first thought.
The value of.
Completely.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Exempt' here does not mean only exempt from the wheat. רבה בר נתן says the defendant pays nothing at all, even for the barley he admitted.

phrases.english: If only from there, I would have said:
he is exempt from the value of wheat,
but liable for the value of barley.
He teaches us that he is completely exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the statement clarifies the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Exempt only from the wheat, but still liable for the barley.
steps.terutzMaskana: Completely exempt, even from the barley.

steps.title: Our משנה seems to make the defendant pay what he admits
steps.stepSummary: In our משנה about two damaged oxen, the ניזק without proof still collects what the מזיק admits. But that looks like wheat and barley, where the defendant should be fully exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if the damaged animals were two, one big and one small, etc. So if he doesn't bring proof, he takes what the מזיק says. Why? This is like wheat and barley!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה בר נתן from our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ניזק claims one thing (the big ox damaged the big one). The מזיק admits something different (the small ox damaged the big one). That is just like claiming wheat and admitting barley. By רבה בר נתן the מזיק should pay nothing, yet the משנה implies the ניזק collects what the מזיק admits.

keyTerms.meaning: The damaged ones.
Proof.
Why?

phrases.english: We learned:
If the damaged animals were two,
one big and one small, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה: each side names a different ox as the one that did the damage, and the ניזק must bring proof.

phrases.english: This implies: if he does not bring proof,
he takes according to what the damager says;
Why?
They are wheat and barley!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבה בר נתן means completely exempt, the גמרא challenges that rule from our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר נתן's rule that the defendant is completely exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies the ניזק collects what the מזיק admits. But the admission is about a different ox than the one claimed, just like barley versus wheat, so by רבה בר נתן the מזיק should pay nothing.

steps.title: He is only fit to take, but does not actually get
steps.stepSummary: The משנה does not mean the ניזק collects. It means he is 'fit to take' the payment, but in practice he gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is fit to take, but he does not have it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 25. It says the משנה never meant that the ניזק actually collects what the מזיק admits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 the משנה seemed to say the ניזק collects according to the מזיק's version. The גמרא now reads it more weakly: he has a fair right to that money, but the court does not force the מזיק to pay it. So רבה בר נתן's 'wheat and barley' rule still holds, and the מזיק is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to take; he has a fair right to it
But he does not have it; the court does not give it to him

steps.confusionAlert: 'Fit to take' does not mean the court makes the מזיק pay. It only means the ניזק deserves it in principle.

phrases.english: He is fit to take
but he does not have it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25 against רבה בר נתן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the משנה: the משנה speaks of a right in principle, not actual collection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means the ניזק actually collects what the מזיק admits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ניזק is only 'fit to take'; the court does not make the מזיק pay, so רבה בר נתן stands.

steps.title: A ברייתא says he does get paid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the ניזק is paid for his small ox from the big ox and for his big ox from the small ox, which sounds like real collection.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: he is paid for the small one from the big one, and for the big one from the small one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 26 with a ברייתא. The ברייתא sounds like the ניזק really collects according to the מזיק's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 said the ניזק is only 'fit to take' and gets nothing. But the ברייתא uses the word 'משתלם', 'he is paid', which sounds like actual payment. So it seems the ניזק does collect.

keyTerms.meaning: He is paid
The small ox / the big ox

phrases.english: But it is taught: this one is paid
for the small one from the big one,
and for the big one from the small one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי זֶה מִשְׁתַּלֵּם עַל הַקָּטָן מִן הַגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 26 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ניזק is only 'fit to take' and receives nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'he is paid', which means actual payment, against step 26.

steps.title: The ברייתא is a case where he grabbed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks about a ניזק who already grabbed the ox. Then the court leaves it with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he grabbed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the ברייתא in one word: it is talking about a case where the ניזק already seized the ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ניזק is 'fit to take' (step 26), if he already grabbed the ox the court does not take it back from him. But the court will not force the מזיק to pay from the start. So the ברייתא and step 26 fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: Where he grabbed (seized it)
Seizing property on one's own

steps.whatToRemember: 'Fit to take' means: the court won't make the מזיק pay, but if the ניזק already grabbed it, he may keep it.

phrases.english: Where he seized.
phrases.notes: The ניזק already took hold of the ox himself, so the court leaves it with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the ברייתא speaks of a ניזק who already seized.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means the court makes the מזיק pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only where the ניזק grabbed; then he keeps it, since he is 'fit to take'.

steps.title: The same problem from the case of a תם and a מועד
steps.stepSummary: In the משנה's next case, one ox is a תם and one a מועד. The ניזק and מזיק disagree about which ox hurt which, yet the ניזק seems to collect by the מזיק's version. But that is wheat and barley!
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If one was a תם and one a מועד, and the ניזק says: 'The מועד hurt the big one and the תם hurt the small one,' and the מזיק says: 'No, the תם hurt the big one and the מועד hurt the small one,' then the one who wants to take from his friend must bring proof. This means if he does not bring proof, he takes what the מזיק says. But why? It is wheat and barley!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רבה בר נתן from the later part of the same משנה. Again the ניזק seems to collect what the מזיק admits, even though his own claim was different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מועד pays full damage and a תם pays only half, so it matters which ox hurt which. The ניזק claimed one pairing and the מזיק admitted a different one, so the admission is like admitting barley when he was sued for wheat. Yet the משנה implies the ניזק collects by the מזיק's version, which goes against רבה בר נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox that has not yet shown a pattern of goring; pays half damage
An ox that was warned as a gorer; pays full damage
The one who wants to take from his friend must bring proof
Wheat and barley; a claim of one thing met with an admission of another
He takes

steps.confusionAlert: Right now the גמרא is only raising the same kind of question from a different case in the משנה. Its answer comes on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: הָיָה אֶחָד תָּם וְאֶחָד מוּעָד,
phrases.english: We learned: If one was a תם and one was a מועד,
and the injured party says:
'The מועד hurt the big one,'
'and the תם hurt the small one,'
and the one who did damage says: 'Not so,'
'rather the תם hurt the big one,'
'and the מועד hurt the small one'
the one who takes from his friend must bring proof.
So if he does not bring proof,
he takes according to what the מזיק says.
But why? It is wheat and barley!
phrases.notes: This points back to רבה בר נתן's rule in step 22: claimed wheat, admitted barley, fully exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הָיָה אֶחָד תָּם וְאֶחָד מוּעָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first-clause challenge was answered, the גמרא brings the same challenge from the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר נתן's rule that claiming wheat and admitting barley makes the defendant fully exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that without proof the ניזק collects by the מזיק's version. But the מזיק admitted something different from the claim, so by רבה בר נתן he should pay nothing.
